scope: Topology-stage structural-orphan detection only. It does not validate TABI claim generation, evidence support, novelty, or research-gap usefulness.

design.baseline_partition_source: Louvain on the unmasked graph using the configured fixed random state

target_selection.policy: all baseline Louvain communities meeting the configured size rule and supporting every same-count control
target_selection.why_not_20_to_30_targets: The configured 5% size rule yields fewer than 20 eligible communities in this run; all eligible, control-feasible communities were used instead.

masking.unit: undirected adjacency; all reciprocal directed arcs for a sampled adjacency are removed together
masking.rounding: ceil(level * target boundary-adjacency count); actual fraction is recorded per trial

measurements.metric_only: Holds the baseline Louvain membership fixed and reapplies the size/bridge-ratio detector after masking.
measurements.end_to_end: Reruns Louvain after masking, then matches output clusters to baseline communities.

matching.rule: Descending-Jaccard greedy one-to-one matching; ties break by overlap, detected size, detected ID, then baseline ID.
matching.precision_labeling: Only deliberately boundary-masked target communities are positives. Every other detected orphan output is a false positive, including a match to a non-target baseline community.

negative_controls: Removes the same number of target-internal adjacencies while retaining all target boundary adjacencies; no induced positives.
Removes the same number of uniformly sampled graph adjacencies without targeting a community boundary; no induced positives.

intervals.metric_intervals: 2,000-resample percentile bootstrap over unique perturbations, not repeated identical seed trials.
intervals.rate_intervals: Wilson 95% intervals; descriptive because target communities derive from this single graph.

limitations: Targets originate from the baseline Louvain partition, so this is a conditional perturbation robustness test rather than an external ground-truth benchmark.
Only three communities satisfy the configured 5% size rule in this run; results cannot establish population-level generalization.
Masked edges are observed graph adjacencies, not verified missing scientific relations.
The negative controls test structural specificity under graph perturbation; they do not validate downstream TABI text generation.
Repeated seeds can yield the same finite edge mask. Primary summaries and bootstrap intervals deduplicate identical perturbations to avoid treating repetitions as independent samples.
